title: RadiANT A/B baseline
description: One bench sitting, one backend, one rig. Phase 4 records these against sdk-ant; Phase 5 onward records them against radiant_core and tools/ant_ab.py diffs the two. Units are in the field names. See README.md in this directory before filling one in.

schema_version.description: Bump only for a breaking change. A reader that does not recognise the value must refuse rather than guess.

radio_runs.description: tools/ant_verify.py results. The Tier 2 loss, timing, accumulator and acquisition gates all read from here.

usb_runs.description: tools/ant_bench.py results. USB round-trip latency and throughput; the radio is not on this path, so equality with sdk-ant is the expectation rather than a stretch.

notes.description: Anything the numbers do not say. Interference seen, a run discarded and why, a cable changed mid-sitting. Prose here is worth more than a rerun later.

recorded.description: ISO 8601 date or date-time the sitting took place. Not the date the file was committed.

operator.description: Who ran it. A bench result with no operator cannot be asked a follow-up question.

backend.description: Which radio backend was under test. Must match CONFIG_ANT_DONGLE_RADIO_* in the built .config.

git_describe.description: Output of `git describe --always --dirty` for this repository at build time. A `-dirty` suffix is allowed and is itself information.

board.description: Zephyr board target of the device under test, e.g. adafruit_feather_nrf52840/nrf52840/uf2.

serial_suffix.description: The --serial suffix that selected this board. Two boards here enumerate as the same 0FCF:1009, so a result with no serial cannot be attributed.

sdk_ant_revision.description: sdk-ant revision linked into the image, e.g. v2.1.0. Null for a core or stub build.

ncs_version.description: nRF Connect SDK version, e.g. v3.2.4.

toolchain_bundle.description: NCS toolchain bundle id, e.g. dcbdc366a1. The bundles are not interchangeable.

extra_conf.description: EXTRA_CONF_FILE fragments applied to the build, in order.

rig.description: The physical arrangement. Two results are only comparable if their rigs are, which is why this is required and why A/B/A must run in one sitting.

second_stack.description: What else was linked into the image under test AND actually transmitting. Part of the rig rather than of the coexistence block because rig equality is what tools/ant_ab.py checks BEFORE any gate runs, and a thread_med sitting and a ble sitting are different experiments however similar their numbers look. `none` is the honest value for an arbitrated build with nothing else on the radio; it is NOT the same as omitting the field, which says the sitting predates the question. Note that `none` says nothing about MPSL: on nRF54L the 802.15.4 driver turns multiprotocol arbitration on by itself, so there is no such thing as an unarbitrated arm on that part - see coexistence.arbiter_note.

kind.description: sim_firmware is sim/ on the nRF54L15 DK running Garmin's certified profile code, and is the reference transmitter. real_sensor is a commercial ANT+ device. ant_sim_py is host-driven and is NOT acceptable as a baseline transmitter - see archive/captures/README.md.

seed.description: Noise seed. A measurement that cannot be replayed is not a measurement.

tx_power_level.description: ANT radio TX power level 0-5, or null if not set explicitly.

antenna.description: Chip, MIFA PCB, external whip. The Feather's ground plane is one of the reasons this project exists; record it.

kind.description: inline_attenuator is preferred and repeatable. fixed_open_air is the fallback, and only comparable within one sitting.

sensitivity_method.description: How the sensitivity ladder applied its dB, mirroring sensitivity.method. It lives in the rig as well as in the measurement because rig equality is what tools/ant_ab.py checks BEFORE any gate runs: a tx_ladder result and a distance result describe different experiments, and the refusal belongs at the sitting rather than inside one gate's detail line. Null on a sitting with no sensitivity ladder.

attenuation_db.description: Fixed attenuation for the non-sensitivity runs, if any.

rf_channel.description: ANT RF channel index; 57 is the ANT+ default (2457 MHz).

interference.description: What else was on the band. The characterised ~0.4% loss floor is memoryless collision with Wi-Fi channel 11 over 2457 MHz, so 'Wi-Fi ch 11 present' is a load-bearing observation, not colour.

profile.description: Profile name as tools/ant_pages.py PROFILES keys it: power, power-torque, power-torque-freq, csc.

seconds.description: Run length. 300 is the gate length; shorter runs do not wrap the slow accumulators and their loss resolution is coarse.

channels.description: How many channels were open. 1 unless this is the 32-channel scale run.

verify.description: Verbatim `tools/ant_verify.py --json` output for this run, embedded whole. Do not hand-edit and do not trim: the fields nobody thinks to keep are the ones a future question needs.

capture.description: Path, relative to the repository root, of the .antcap recorded alongside - normally under archive/captures/radio/. A run with a capture can be re-analysed after a decoder fix; one without cannot.

derived.description: The handful of numbers the gates in tools/ab_gates.toml read. All are also present inside `verify`; they are lifted out so a gate runner does not have to know that object's shape.

loss_pct.description: The wall-clock loss figure. Recorded, but not the one to gate on.

loss_exact_pct.description: Loss counted from the transmitter's own event counter, with no clock involved. THIS is the gate. The bench floor is characterised at 0.26-0.60%.

unexplained_loss.description: Holes with no RX_FAIL to account for them. Must be 0. This is the check that caught the reader bug; a nonzero value invalidates the whole sitting rather than failing one gate.

timing_offgrid_host_ms.description: The `timing` line: intervals minus whole periods, on the host clock. Expect ~2.6 ms. NOT the `jitter` line, which is a stddev over raw gaps and turns one lost packet into 500 ms.

timing_offgrid_radio_ms.description: The same measured on the radio's clock via lib config 0xE0's RX timestamp. Expect ~0.009 ms. This is the number that shows the host clock is the instrument, not the link.

reacquire_s.description: Time to re-acquire after a deliberate dropout. Gate is <= sdk-ant x 1.5 and <= 5 s absolute.

sched_missed.description: Receive windows the dongle's scheduler declared DONE_MISSED - it could not arm them in time, so the radio never listened in them. Read out of the firmware by tools/ant_health.py (MESG_RADIANT_HEALTH, needs CONFIG_ANT_DONGLE_HEALTH_COUNTERS=y) before and after the run, and recorded as the delta. Must be 0. It is a scheduling artefact rather than an air measurement, which makes it the one loss-shaped gate a noisy room cannot move - and it is structurally zero at one channel, so read it on the multi-channel runs.

per_channel.description: Per-channel figures from a multi-channel run, keyed by receive channel number as a string - `tools/ant_verify.py`'s own `derived.per_channel`, copied across. Recorded, not gated: a scheduler that drops the later of two nearby receive windows costs one channel of a pair and leaves the other alone, so the pooled loss figure beside this one halves the effect and only the spread across channels shows it. Absent on the single-channel runs, which is every baseline recorded before 2026-08-15.

coexistence.description: What a second protocol stack on the same radio costs, from ONE sitting on ONE build. Every other block here is half of an A-versus-B comparison across two backends; this one is not, and that is why it is a block of its own. Its three loss figures are the same backend measured three ways minutes apart - direct gate, arbitrated with the second stack off, arbitrated with it on - and they are only comparable to each other because they came off the same board without the rig being touched. tools/ant_ab.py gate_coexistence() reads exactly the fields below.

second_stack.description: Which stack was contending. Must equal rig.second_stack; it is repeated here so a coexistence block lifted out of its file still says what it measured.

loss_direct_pct.description: `loss (exact)` on the DIRECT-gate build - no arbiter at all. The reference for the arbiter's own cost, which is the exit criterion for the whole combined build. Null where the part cannot build a direct arm: on nRF54L the 802.15.4 radio driver enables MPSL by itself, so an image with 15.4 in it is arbitrated whether or not this project asked for it, and there is no honest direct number to record.

loss_second_stack_off_pct.description: `loss (exact)` on the arbitrated build with the second stack linked in but NOT transmitting - the arbiter present and no competitor. THE ARM THAT MAKES THIS A MEASUREMENT, and the one this project has already got wrong once: `CONFIG_BT=y` alone linked a controller in and left it asleep, and the gate came back with a sweep ratio of exactly 1.000 - a gate that cannot fail. Read the pair off/on as 'what the demand cost', never as 'what arbitration cost'.

loss_second_stack_on_pct.description: `loss (exact)` on the same build with the second stack actually carrying traffic. Record thread_load_sent beside it or the figure is not a measurement.

sweep_sets_per_s_off.description: Discovery sweep rate with the second stack off, from CONFIG_RADIANT_CORE_SWEEP_DEBUG. The sweep is the elastic consumer (ADR 0013) so it IS the thing that gives way; bounded rather than accepted, because 'the sweep gives way' with no number attached is indistinguishable from a sweep that stopped.

thread_load_sent.description: `sent=` from src/thread_coex_load.c over the ON arm. A P4 number quoted without it is not a measurement: an attached MTD that transmitted nothing looks exactly like perfect coexistence.

scheduler_cost.description: THE OTHER HALF OF THE RESULT, and the half docs/radiant-bridge.md 7.3a says the docs record nowhere. The loss figures above are the AIR cost - what ANT+ lost. This is what the reserve cost the OTHER stack's scheduler, which 7.3a asserts is where the cost actually lands. Recorded per arm because a delta against the ANT-idle arm is the whole point; a single number would be unreadable.

send_latency_us_max_ant_idle.description: Worst zsock_sendto() latency with ANT placing no windows. The reference arm - an arm whose other stack is idle is not a coexistence arm, and this is the number that proves this one was not.

send_latency_us_p99_ant_idle.description: Interpolated from the logarithmic buckets src/thread_coex_load.c prints, so it carries the buckets' resolution and no more. A mean is deliberately not recorded: the scheduler cost is a tail, and averaging the sends that landed inside a grant with the ones that did not produces a number true of neither.

mac_tx_retry_ant_idle.description: otLinkGetCounters() deltas over the arm. These ARE deferral measured on the other stack's own terms: a CCA failure or a retry is the 15.4 MAC finding the air taken, and under this build it is very often taken by us. They are the Thread-side mirror of the gate's own ext=a/b.

gate_counters.description: The 1 Hz gate dump at the end of the ON arm. grant_end_calls tracking granted is the invariant the whole grant-abort work exists to defend, and late_disarm/overstayed/invalid_return must all be zero - a non-zero late_disarm names a fault that otherwise presents only as a receiver that stopped hours ago.

arbiter_note.description: What this sitting could NOT isolate, in prose, and it is required reading rather than colour. On nRF54L there is no build of the 15.4 driver without MPSL, so an arm with the second stack merely linked in is 15.4-with-an-arbiter-and-no-competitor - it measures what a second stack's DEMAND costs, not what arbitration costs. Say so here rather than letting the off/on delta be read as the arbiter's price.

conformance.description: Tier 1. The acceptance criterion is a byte diff of two .antser files, so what is recorded here is a path and a hash, not a score.

antser_path.description: Path relative to the repository root, normally under archive/captures/serial/.

byte_identical_to.description: sha256 of the reference transcript this one was diffed against, or null when this IS the reference.

sensitivity.description: The attenuated-link curve. This is the slot that must not be left empty: sensitivity is a stated core value of the project, it is the figure the EFR32 question turns on, and it cannot be recovered after sdk-ant access lapses.

method.description: Same transmitter, same rig, receivers swapped. An open-air path is only comparable within one sitting. tx_ladder is tools/ant_sens.py: the master's transmit power stepped down to the receiver's knee, which is the same attenuation applied at the far end of the link and the only one of the three that needs no hardware this bench does not have. The three carry different systematic offsets and are never converted between; tools/ant_ab.py refuses a comparison across two methods.

steps.description: One entry per attenuation setting, distance or transmit power, monotonically increasing in attenuation - so decreasing in tx_power_dbm.

tx_power_dbm.description: Commanded transmit power for a tx_ladder step. Commanded, not measured - which is why tools/ant_sens.py fits measured RSSI against it and refuses the ladder if the two disagree.

loss_basis.description: Which counter the loss figure came from. event_counter is the transmitter's own, via ant_verify.py, and is the one the name promises. master_sent is the host's count of what it handed the transmitter, used only past the knee where too little of the stream survives to read the counter out of it at all.

loss5pct_attenuation_db.description: Interpolated attenuation at 5% exact loss. This single number is what the gate compares, to within 1 dB-equivalent on the same rig.

loss5pct_tx_power_dbm.description: The tx_ladder equivalent: interpolated transmit power at 5% exact loss. LOWER IS BETTER here, the opposite of attenuation and distance - a receiver that still works with a quieter transmitter hears better. tools/ant_ab.py carries that sign per key rather than per gate. Null when the ladder did not contain the crossing, which is a refusal to extrapolate and not a missing measurement.

loss5pct_rssi_dbm.description: The same knee expressed as power at the receiver rather than at the transmitter, which is the figure that means something off this bench. Derived from a reference rung well above the knee minus the dB walked down from it - never read off the knee rung's own RSSI, whose survivors are biased high by exactly the thing being measured.

repeat_spread_db.description: Spread of the 5% point across repeated ladders on an unchanged rig. This is the instrument's own noise, and gates.sensitivity.repeat_max_delta_db is the Phase 0 acceptance test: an instrument that cannot repeat to 1 dB cannot grade a 1 dB claim.

scale.description: The 32-channel run. An absolute gate, not a relative one: libant.a cannot reach 32 channels, so there is no sdk-ant baseline to compare against and none should be invented.

per_channel_loss_pct.description: Worst per-channel exact loss across the tracked set.

single_channel_loss_pct.description: The same rig with one channel, for the +0.5 pp comparison.

background_scan.description: Did a wildcard scan-mode channel hear every sensor ant_scan.py finds? Also absolute - libant.a advertises scan mode off and does not implement it.

ack_data.description: Acknowledged-data success, which is ERG mode: Zwift setting trainer resistance. Gate is >= 99% and >= sdk-ant - 1 pp.
